summary: Emi Matsushita, a history and archaeology scholar, studied at Nanzan University, the University of East Anglia, and Ohio State University under MA supervisor John C. Huntington. She held posts at the Shizuoka Prefectural Board of Education and Ohio State.

Emil Rödiger was a scholar of linguistics and religious studies who earned his Dr. phil. and Lic. theol. from the University of Halle-Wittenberg. He held professorships at Halle-Wittenberg (1830–1860) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1860).
Emil Schlagintweit worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under tutor Franz Joseph Lauth and became a corresponding member of the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 1864.

Indologist and linguist Emil Sieg studied at Munich, Tübingen, Kiel, Berlin (PhD under Albrecht Weber), and Göttingen under Franz Kielhorn. He held posts at Berlin, Kiel University (1909; 1918–1919), and the University of Göttingen (from 1920).

Emilio Teza was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Anton Boller. He served as librarian at the Biblioteca Marciana and Laurentian Library before holding professorships at the universities of Bologna (1860), Pisa (~1861–1886), and Padua (~1886–1906).

Emily T. Yeh is a Tibetologist who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and the University of California, Berkeley. She held an academic post at the University of Colorado Boulder beginning around 2003.

Emma Georgina Rothschild is a historian who studied at Somerville College and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. She held professorships at the University of Cambridge around 2000 and at Harvard University around 2008.

Indologist Emmie te Nijenhuis studied at Utrecht Conservatory, Utrecht School of the Arts, and Utrecht University, earning her PhD under Jan Gonda. She served as associate professor of Indian musicology at Utrecht University (1964–1988) and at Amsterdam.

Enamul Haque was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at the University of Dhaka and Oxford. He served as Director General of the Bangladesh National Museum (1983–1991) and professor at Independent University, Bangladesh (~2002–2022).

Encho Tamura was a Buddhist studies and history scholar who studied at Kyushu and Kyoto universities. He held academic posts at Kyushu University, Kumamoto University (~1975–1982), and directorships at the Kyushu Historical Museum and Fukuoka Human Rights Center.

Endō Asai was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Rissho University. He held teaching posts at Minobusan Senmon Gakko, Nihon Fukushi University, Rissho University, and served as president of Minobusan University (1998–2002).
Eng Jin Ooi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at Mahidol University by 2021, supervised by Giuliano Giustarini, Peter Skilling, and Kengo Harimoto.
Enga Teramoto, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studied at Kumbum Monastery in 1903. He later held academic posts at Otani University (from 1915) and Kyoto University (~1923–1930).

Enichi Ocho was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at the University of Tokyo under Daijo Tokiwa. He worked at the Academy of Oriental Culture (1931) and served as professor emeritus at Otani University (1949–1976).

Enryo Inoue was a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Ernest Fenollosa and Tanzan Hara. He founded Toyo University, serving as lecturer and manager (~1887–1905), and founded several schools.

Ensho Kanakura was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Tohoku University (1926–1960) and Rissho University (~1958–1974), and served as president of Miyagi University of Education (1967).
Ensho Kobayashi is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Hanazono University as a professor (attested 1988) and later as professor emeritus (attested 2026).
Ensho Nasu is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at Ryukoku University (attested 1996) under the supervision of Esho Mikogami.

Enshu Kurumiya is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who earned a PhD from the Australian National University in 1974. Kurumiya served as a professor of Buddhist studies at Rissho University (attested 1981–1985).

Erberto Lo Bue was a Tibetology and history scholar who earned a PhD from SOAS University of London (~1976–1981). He lectured in Tibetan at the University of Milan (~1993–1999) and held a post at the University of Bologna (~2000–2016).
